newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania to launch battle against polio.
newsitem.headline: Albania to launch battle against polio.

text.p: Albania and international organisations were poised on Tuesday to launch an ambitious immunisation campaign to battle a rampant polio virus from spreading further through this impoverished Balkan nation.
Albania's World Health Organisation (WHO) liaison officer Vladimir Gusmari said vaccines would arrive by ferry from Bari, Italy, on October 3.
"We hope the immunisation campaign will last from seven to 10 days," Gusmari said, adding the first stage of immunisation with some 3.5 million doses would start immediately.
The polio outbreak, which has spread among adults, is believed to have killed 12 people so far, with about 90 reported to have contracted the virus, according to unofficial sources.
The immunisation drive was aimed primarily at Albanians up to the age of 50.

"The second stage encompasses booster doses to reinforce and achieve lifelong immunity," Gusmari said. "Albanians should understand the vaccine is necessary because of the virulent virus in the country."
The outbreak started in April in the northwestern part of Albania and then fanned out to the capital Tirana and the rest of the country.
Gusmari said a sub-standard vaccination made in Albania and dating back to the 1960s was largely to blame for the outbreak.
